The test image shows a corn plant with one leaf that has turned completely white/bleached and papery, while surrounding leaves remain green. This blanched, papery appearance is distinctive. Top candidates: Crazy_Top (downy mildew can cause leaf bleaching), or possibly Goss_S_Wilt.

Let me check the Crazy_Top reference.

The Crazy_Top reference shows distorted tassels with proliferating structures — quite different from the test image. The test shows a single completely white/bleached papery leaf while the rest of the plant is green.

This bleached-white leaf appearance is more consistent with **Goss's Wilt**, where bacterial blight can cause entire leaves to bleach white/tan in advanced stages. The pattern of one leaf dying while the plant otherwise looks intact also fits.
